# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

# Employees

Generated employee profiles live here. Every store gets the same fixed roster shape:

- one `General Store Manager` with roles `employee`, `store_manager`, `discount_manager`, `refund_manager`, `inventory_viewer`, `fulfillment_viewer`, and `customer_service`
- one `Inventory Specialist` with roles `employee`, `inventory_specialist`, `inventory_viewer`, and `stock_adjuster`
- one `Fulfillment Coordinator` with roles `employee`, `fulfillment_coordinator`, `fulfillment_operator`, and `inventory_viewer`
- two `Customer Service Associate` employees with roles `employee`, `customer_service`, `order_viewer`, and `discount_requester`

Employee records include `email`, `roles`, and `title` for identity and authorization lookup tasks.

# Baskets

Generated customer baskets live here. Basket files list customer, store, lifecycle status, and requested line items.

Basket records include `created_at`, generated from world time, so tasks can refer to basket recency such as "the last basket".

Baskets do not carry availability flags; compare basket lines with store inventory when checkout eligibility matters.

Discounted baskets carry a `discount` object with `percent`, `reason_code`, and `issuer_id`.

Basket status is lifecycle state. `active` baskets may still need inventory checks before checkout; `checked_out` baskets are historical orders and may have linked records under `/proc/payments/` and `/proc/returns/`.

# Customers

Generated customer profiles live here. The customer id from `/bin/id` can be matched against these records.

Customer records include `email` for contact identity and lookup tasks. `home_lat` and `home_lon` are coarse generated home-area coordinates used by payment-risk fixtures.

# Payments

Generated payment records live here. Current payment files represent one payment attempt for a `checked_out` basket.

Older payments may have `basket_archived: true`. Those basket records have aged out of `/proc/baskets/` into cold storage, so the payment file carries its own `lines` snapshot with SKU, quantity, and unit price.

Payment statuses are compact:

- `paid`: payment completed successfully.
- `requires_3ds_action`: payment is stuck in the simulated 3DS workflow.

Stuck payments include a `three_ds` object with legacy challenge status, failure reason, attempts, and maximum attempts. The `three_ds.status` values intentionally use inherited 3DS codes; consult the payment policy before deciding whether a payment can be recovered.

Payment fingerprints are opaque instrument/device identifiers. `observed_lat` and `observed_lon` are checkout-time coordinates from the payment risk log, not a customer address.

# Returns

Generated return workflow records live here. Return records only exist for paid checked-out baskets.

Return statuses are compact: `requested`, `approved`, `rejected`, `refund_pending`, `replacement_pending`, and `closed`.

Use `payment_id`, `basket_id`, and `customer_id` to reconcile a return with the linked payment and checked-out basket.

# Store Network Notes



Team,

Here is the short version of how the PowerTool Central Europe branch map got to its current shape.

We started with the Vienna Praterstern branch in 2017, serving trade customers who needed a central Vienna pickup point near the rail hub. The Vienna Meidling branch followed in 2019 after west-side crews kept losing time crossing town; when a customer says the west-side Vienna PowerTool shop, they mean Meidling, not Praterstern.

Graz came next. Jakomini opened in 2020 as our central Graz store, close enough to the inner-city job sites to act as the default Graz branch. Lend opened in 2022 to cover the north side of Graz and the routes coming in from that direction. In Graz language, north Graz means Lend; central Graz means Jakomini.

In 2023 we added Linz Hauptplatz and Salzburg Elisabeth-Vorstadt. Linz is the main-square branch. Salzburg Elisabeth-Vorstadt is the station-side branch, so local notes may call it the shop near Salzburg station.

In 2024 we opened Innsbruck Wilten and Bratislava Stare Mesto. Wilten is our central Innsbruck store for practical dispatch purposes. Stare Mesto is the old-town Bratislava branch.

The newest 2025 additions are Brno Veveri and Ljubljana Center. Veveri is our central Brno branch. Ljubljana Center is the downtown Ljubljana shop.

When several stores share a city, use the city nuance above before checking inventory. Inventory itself remains in the SQL projection, keyed by the store IDs from the JSON files in this directory.

Store JSON records include generated branch coordinates for payment-risk and distance checks.

customer_accounts,"CREATE TABLE customer_accounts (
	customer_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
	record_path TEXT NOT NULL,
	customer_display_name TEXT NOT NULL,
	customer_email TEXT NOT NULL,
	home_city TEXT NOT NULL,
	home_latitude REAL NOT NULL,
	home_longitude REAL NOT NULL
)"
employee_accounts,"CREATE TABLE employee_accounts (
	employee_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
	record_path TEXT NOT NULL,
	employee_display_name TEXT NOT NULL,
	employee_email TEXT NOT NULL,
	job_title TEXT NOT NULL,
	store_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES stores(store_id)
)"
employee_role_assignments,"CREATE TABLE employee_role_assignments (
	employee_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	role_code TEXT NOT NULL,
	PRIMARY KEY (employee_id, role_code),
	FOREIGN KEY (employee_id) REFERENCES employee_accounts(employee_id)
)"
payment_transaction_items,"CREATE TABLE payment_transaction_items (
	payment_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	line_number INTEGER NOT NULL,
	product_sku TEXT NOT NULL,
	purchased_quantity INTEGER NOT NULL,
	item_unit_price_cents INTEGER NOT NULL,
	PRIMARY KEY (payment_id, line_number),
	FOREIGN KEY (payment_id) REFERENCES payment_transactions(payment_id),
	FOREIGN KEY (product_sku) REFERENCES product_variants(product_sku)
)"
payment_transactions,"CREATE TABLE payment_transactions (
	payment_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
	record_path TEXT NOT NULL,
	basket_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	is_archived_basket_reference INTEGER NOT NULL,
	customer_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	store_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	payment_amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL,
	payment_currency TEXT NOT NULL,
	payment_status TEXT NOT NULL,
	payment_created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
	payment_method_fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL,
	device_fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL,
	observed_latitude REAL NOT NULL,
	observed_longitude REAL NOT NULL,
	three_ds_status TEXT,
	three_ds_failure_reason TEXT,
	three_ds_attempts INTEGER,
	three_ds_max_attempts INTEGER,
	FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customer_accounts(customer_id),
	FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES stores(store_id)
)"
product_categories,"CREATE TABLE product_categories (
	product_category_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
	product_category_name TEXT NOT NULL,
	product_department TEXT NOT NULL
)"
product_families,"CREATE TABLE product_families (
	product_family_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
	product_category_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	product_kind_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	brand TEXT NOT NULL,
	series TEXT NOT NULL,
	model TEXT NOT NULL,
	product_family_name TEXT NOT NULL,
	properties TEXT NOT NULL
)"
product_kinds,"CREATE TABLE product_kinds (
	product_kind_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
	product_category_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	product_kind_name TEXT NOT NULL
)"
product_variant_properties,"CREATE TABLE product_variant_properties (
	product_sku TEXT NOT NULL,
	property_key TEXT NOT NULL,
	property_value_text TEXT NOT NULL,
	property_value_number REAL,
	PRIMARY KEY (product_sku, property_key)
)"
product_variants,"CREATE TABLE product_variants (
	product_sku TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
	record_path TEXT NOT NULL,
	product_category_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	product_kind_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	product_family_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	brand TEXT NOT NULL,
	series TEXT NOT NULL,
	model TEXT NOT NULL,
	product_name TEXT NOT NULL,
	price_cents INTEGER NOT NULL,
	price_currency TEXT NOT NULL,
	properties TEXT NOT NULL
)"
return_requests,"CREATE TABLE return_requests (
	return_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
	record_path TEXT NOT NULL,
	basket_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	customer_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	payment_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	return_status TEXT NOT NULL,
	return_reason_code TEXT NOT NULL,
	return_created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
	FOREIGN KEY (basket_id) REFERENCES shopping_baskets(basket_id),
	FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customer_accounts(customer_id),
	FOREIGN KEY (payment_id) REFERENCES payment_transactions(payment_id)
)"
shopping_basket_items,"CREATE TABLE shopping_basket_items (
	basket_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	line_number INTEGER NOT NULL,
	product_sku TEXT NOT NULL,
	requested_quantity INTEGER NOT NULL,
	PRIMARY KEY (basket_id, line_number),
	FOREIGN KEY (basket_id) REFERENCES shopping_baskets(basket_id),
	FOREIGN KEY (product_sku) REFERENCES product_variants(product_sku)
)"
shopping_baskets,"CREATE TABLE shopping_baskets (
	basket_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
	record_path TEXT NOT NULL,
	customer_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	store_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	basket_status TEXT NOT NULL,
	basket_created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
	discount_percent INTEGER,
	discount_reason_code TEXT,
	discount_issuer_employee_id TEXT,
	FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customer_accounts(customer_id),
	FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES stores(store_id)
)"
store_inventory,"CREATE TABLE store_inventory (
	store_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	product_sku TEXT NOT NULL,
	on_hand_quantity INTEGER NOT NULL,
	reserved_quantity INTEGER NOT NULL,
	available_today_quantity INTEGER NOT NULL,
	incoming_quantity INTEGER NOT NULL,
	next_arrival_in_days INTEGER,
	PRIMARY KEY (store_id, product_sku),
	FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES stores(store_id),
	FOREIGN KEY (product_sku) REFERENCES product_variants(product_sku)
)"
stores,"CREATE TABLE stores (
	store_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
	record_path TEXT NOT NULL,
	store_name TEXT NOT NULL,
	city TEXT NOT NULL,
	is_open INTEGER NOT NULL,
	latitude REAL NOT NULL,
	longitude REAL NOT NULL
)"

# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

response.content:
# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

	store_id TEXT NOT NULL,

product_categories,table,"CREATE TABLE product_categories (

product_families,table,"CREATE TABLE product_families (

	series TEXT NOT NULL,
	model TEXT NOT NULL,

product_kinds,table,"CREATE TABLE product_kinds (

product_variant_properties,table,"CREATE TABLE product_variant_properties (

# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.

WITH target_store AS (
  SELECT store_id, record_path FROM stores WHERE store_id='store_vienna_praterstern'
), req AS (
  SELECT 1 AS req_id, 'Heco' AS brand, 'GTU-YPJ' AS model, 'Wood and Drywall Screw' AS kind, 'screw_type' AS k1, 'wood screw' AS v1, 'diameter' AS k2, '6 mm' AS v2
  UNION ALL SELECT 2,'Ajax','25C-DXE','Cleaning Liquid','cleaner_type','floor cleaner',NULL,NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 3,'Heco','GTU-YPJ','Wood and Drywall Screw','screw_type','wood screw','diameter','3 mm'
  UNION ALL SELECT 4,'Heco','3DW-64B','Nut Bolt and Washer','fastener_type','threaded rod',NULL,NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 5,'Festool','3JJ-9LM','Tool Box and Bag','storage_type','tool bag',NULL,NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 6,'Heco','GTU-YPJ','Wood and Drywall Screw','screw_type','wood screw','diameter','6 mm'
), matched AS (
  SELECT r.req_id, pv.product_sku, pv.record_path, si.available_today_quantity
  FROM req r
  JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.brand=r.brand AND pv.model=r.model AND pv.product_name LIKE '%'||r.kind||'%'
  JOIN product_kinds pk ON pk.product_kind_id=pv.product_kind_id AND pk.product_kind_name=r.kind
  JOIN product_variant_properties p1 ON p1.product_sku=pv.product_sku AND p1.property_key=r.k1
  LEFT JOIN product_variant_properties p2 ON p2.product_sku=pv.product_sku AND r.k2 IS NOT NULL AND p2.property_key=r.k2
  JOIN target_store ts
  JOIN store_inventory si ON si.store_id=ts.store_id AND si.product_sku=pv.product_sku
  WHERE lower(replace(p1.property_value_text,' ','')) = lower(replace(r.v1,' ',''))
    AND (r.k2 IS NULL OR lower(replace(p2.property_value_text,' ','')) = lower(replace(r.v2,' ','')))
)
SELECT req_id, product_sku, record_path, available_today_quantity
FROM matched
WHERE available_today_quantity >= 2
ORDER BY req_id, product_sku;

# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

WITH target_store AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM stores
  WHERE city='Graz' AND (name LIKE '%Jakomini%' OR name LIKE '%PowerTool Graz Jakomini%')
  LIMIT 1
), req(label, brand, series_like, model, attr1_key, attr1_val, attr2_key, attr2_val, attr3_key, attr3_val) AS (
  VALUES
  ('lawn_mower','Stihl','%Stihl Classic%','RMA 1TV-KC3','power_source','battery','cutting_width','32 cm',NULL,NULL),
  ('work_trousers','Carhartt','%Carhartt Stretch Rugged%','3EY-11K','color_family','Black','size','M','fit','regular'),
  ('cleaning_machine','Karcher','%Karcher Workshop%','SC 27T-68S','machine_type','pressure washer',NULL,NULL,NULL,NULL),
  ('wall_paint','Helios','%Helios Quick Dry Mobihel%','1VV-8Y1','color_family','Orange',NULL,NULL,NULL,NULL),
  ('work_jacket','Uvex','%Uvex Bionic x-fit%','Y59-F8N','color_family','Yellow','size','XL',NULL,NULL),
  ('cleaning_liquid','Karcher','%Karcher Workshop%','WD 2C4-U0U','cleaner_type','floor cleaner','volume','5000 ml',NULL,NULL)
), matched AS (
  SELECT r.label, p.sku, p.path,
         i.available_today
  FROM req r
  JOIN products p
    ON p.brand = r.brand
   AND p.series LIKE r.series_like
   AND p.model = r.model
   AND (r.attr1_key IS NULL OR lower(replace(json_extract(p.properties, '$.'||r.attr1_key),' ','')) = lower(replace(r.attr1_val,' ','')))
   AND (r.attr2_key IS NULL OR lower(replace(json_extract(p.properties, '$.'||r.attr2_key),' ','')) = lower(replace(r.attr2_val,' ','')))
   AND (r.attr3_key IS NULL OR lower(replace(json_extract(p.properties, '$.'||r.attr3_key),' ','')) = lower(replace(r.attr3_val,' ','')))
  JOIN target_store ts ON 1=1
  LEFT JOIN inventory i
    ON i.store_id = ts.id AND i.sku = p.sku
)
SELECT (SELECT id FROM target_store) AS store_id,
       (SELECT name FROM target_store) AS store_name,
       label, sku, path, available_today
FROM matched
ORDER BY label, sku;

# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

WITH target_store AS (
  SELECT store_id, store_name, record_path
  FROM stores
  WHERE city='Graz' AND store_name LIKE '%Jakomini%'
  LIMIT 1
),
P1 AS (
  SELECT pv.product_sku, pv.record_path, si.available_today_quantity
  FROM product_variants pv
  JOIN target_store ts ON 1=1
  JOIN store_inventory si ON si.store_id=ts.store_id AND si.product_sku=pv.product_sku
  JOIN product_variant_properties a1 ON a1.product_sku=pv.product_sku AND a1.property_key='power_source'
  JOIN product_variant_properties a2 ON a2.product_sku=pv.product_sku AND a2.property_key='cutting_width'
  WHERE pv.brand='Stihl' AND pv.series LIKE '%Stihl Classic%' AND pv.model='RMA 1TV-KC3'
    AND lower(replace(a1.property_value_text,' ',''))=lower(replace('battery',' ',''))

WITH inv AS (
  SELECT pv.product_sku, pv.record_path, pv.brand, pv.series, pv.model, pv.product_kind_id, si.available_today_quantity
  FROM product_variants pv
  JOIN store_inventory si ON si.product_sku = pv.product_sku
  WHERE si.store_id='store_vienna_meidling'
),
q1 AS (
  SELECT 'P1' AS pid, i.product_sku, i.record_path, i.available_today_quantity
  FROM inv i
  JOIN product_kinds pk ON pk.product_kind_id=i.product_kind_id
  WHERE i.brand='Portwest' AND i.series='Portwest PW3 DX 3TU-ST2' AND i.model='3TU-ST2'
    AND pk.product_kind_name='Work Gloves'
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM product_variant_properties p
      WHERE p.product_sku=i.product_sku AND lower(p.property_key)='size' AND lower(replace(p.property_value_text,' ',''))='l'
    )
),
q2 AS (
  SELECT 'P2' AS pid, i.product_sku, i.record_path, i.available_today_quantity
  FROM inv i
  JOIN product_kinds pk ON pk.product_kind_id=i.product_kind_id
  WHERE i.brand='Philips' AND i.series='Philips Professional Hue 3JS-MSN' AND i.model='3JS-MSN'
    AND pk.product_kind_name='LED Bulb'
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM product_variant_properties p
      WHERE p.product_sku=i.product_sku AND lower(p.property_key)='wattage' AND lower(replace(p.property_value_text,' ',''))='10w'
    )
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM product_variant_properties p
      WHERE p.product_sku=i.product_sku AND lower(p.property_key)='luminous flux' AND lower(replace(p.property_value_text,' ',''))='470lm'
    )
),
q3 AS (
  SELECT 'P3' AS pid, i.product_sku, i.record_path, i.available_today_quantity
  FROM inv i
  JOIN product_kinds pk ON pk.product_kind_id=i.product_kind_id
  WHERE i.brand='Engelbert Strauss' AND i.series='Engelbert Strauss Classic e.s. 37H-N9K' AND i.model='37H-N9K'
    AND pk.product_kind_name='Work Trousers'
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM product_variant_properties p
      WHERE p.product_sku=i.product_sku AND lower(p.property_key)='color family' AND lower(p.property_value_text)='blue'
    )
),
q4 AS (
  SELECT 'P4' AS pid, i.product_sku, i.record_path, i.available_today_quantity
  FROM inv i
  JOIN product_kinds pk ON pk.product_kind_id=i.product_kind_id
  WHERE i.brand='Bahco' AND i.series='Bahco Comfort Grip BE 1ZR-PGS' AND i.model='1ZR-PGS'
    AND pk.product_kind_name='Pliers and Wrenches'
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM product_variant_properties p
      WHERE p.product_sku=i.product_sku AND lower(p.property_key)='tool type' AND lower(p.property_value_text)='side cutter'
    )
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM product_variant_properties p
      WHERE p.product_sku=i.product_sku AND lower(p.property_key)='length' AND lower(replace(p.property_value_text,' ',''))='125mm'
    )
),
q5 AS (
  SELECT 'P5' AS pid, i.product_sku, i.record_path, i.available_today_quantity
  FROM inv i
  JOIN product_kinds pk ON pk.product_kind_id=i.product_kind_id
  WHERE i.brand='Bosch' AND i.series='Bosch Compact PKS 375-EOK' AND i.model='375-EOK'
    AND pk.product_kind_name='Corded Angle Grinder'
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM product_variant_properties p
      WHERE p.product_sku=i.product_sku AND lower(p.property_key)='disc diameter' AND lower(replace(p.property_value_text,' ',''))='180mm'
    )
),
q6 AS (
  SELECT 'P6' AS pid, i.product_sku, i.record_path, i.available_today_quantity
  FROM inv i
  JOIN product_kinds pk ON pk.product_kind_id=i.product_kind_id
  WHERE i.brand='Sika' AND i.series='Sika Professional Sika 28T-UV8' AND i.model='28T-UV8'
    AND pk.product_kind_name='Sealant'
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM product_variant_properties p
      WHERE p.product_sku=i.product_sku AND lower(p.property_key)='sealant type' AND lower(p.property_value_text)='silicone sealant'
    )
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM product_variant_properties p
      WHERE p.product_sku=i.product_sku AND lower(p.property_key)='color family' AND lower(p.property_value_text)='clear'
    )
)
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT * FROM q1 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM q2 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM q3
  UNION ALL SELECT * FROM q4 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM q5 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM q6
)
ORDER BY pid, product_sku;

WITH req(pid, brand, model, k1, v1, k2, v2, k3, v3) AS (
  VALUES
  ('P1','Stihl','RMA 1TV-KC3','power_source','battery','cutting_width','32 cm',NULL,NULL),
  ('P2','Carhartt','3EY-11K','color_family','Black','size','M','fit','regular'),
  ('P3','Karcher','SC 27T-68S','machine_type','pressure washer',NULL,NULL,NULL,NULL),
  ('P4','Helios','1VV-8Y1','color_family','Orange',NULL,NULL,NULL,NULL),
  ('P5','Uvex','Y59-F8N','color_family','Yellow','size','XL',NULL,NULL),
  ('P6','Karcher','WD 2C4-U0U','cleaner_type','floor cleaner','volume','5000 ml',NULL,NULL)
), candidates AS (
  SELECT r.pid, pv.product_sku, pv.record_path,
         MAX(CASE WHEN pvp.property_key=r.k1 AND lower(replace(pvp.property_value_text,' ',''))=lower(replace(r.v1,' ','')) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS m1,
         MAX(CASE WHEN r.k2 IS NULL THEN 1 WHEN pvp.property_key=r.k2 AND lower(replace(pvp.property_value_text,' ',''))=lower(replace(r.v2,' ','')) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS m2,
         MAX(CASE WHEN r.k3 IS NULL THEN 1 WHEN pvp.property_key=r.k3 AND lower(replace(pvp.property_value_text,' ',''))=lower(replace(r.v3,' ','')) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS m3
  FROM req r
  JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.brand=r.brand AND pv.model=r.model
  LEFT JOIN product_variant_properties pvp ON pvp.product_sku=pv.product_sku
  GROUP BY r.pid, pv.product_sku, pv.record_path
), matched AS (
  SELECT c.pid, c.product_sku, c.record_path, si.available_today_quantity
  FROM candidates c
  LEFT JOIN store_inventory si ON si.product_sku=c.product_sku AND si.store_id='store_graz_jakomini'
  WHERE c.m1=1 AND c.m2=1 AND c.m3=1
)
SELECT pid, product_sku, record_path, COALESCE(available_today_quantity, -1) AS available_today_quantity
FROM matched
ORDER BY pid, product_sku;

SELECT pv.brand, pv.series, pv.model, pk.product_kind_name, pv.product_sku, pv.record_path, si.available_today_quantity
FROM product_variants pv
JOIN product_kinds pk ON pk.product_kind_id=pv.product_kind_id
JOIN store_inventory si ON si.product_sku=pv.product_sku AND si.store_id='store_vienna_meidling'
WHERE (pv.brand='Portwest' AND pv.model='3TU-ST2')
   OR (pv.brand='Philips' AND pv.model='3JS-MSN')
   OR (pv.brand='Engelbert Strauss' AND pv.model='37H-N9K')
   OR (pv.brand='Bahco' AND pv.model='1ZR-PGS')
   OR (pv.brand='Bosch' AND pv.model='375-EOK')
   OR (pv.brand='Sika' AND pv.model='28T-UV8')
ORDER BY pv.brand, pv.model, pv.product_sku
LIMIT 200;

FROM product_variants
WHERE model IN ('RMA 1TV-KC3','3EY-11K','SC 27T-68S','1VV-8Y1','Y59-F8N','WD 2C4-U0U')
ORDER BY model, product_sku

WITH target_store AS (
  SELECT 'store_vienna_praterstern' AS store_id
),
q1 AS (
  SELECT 1 AS row_id, pv.product_sku, pv.record_path, si.available_today_quantity
  FROM product_variants pv
  JOIN product_variant_properties p1 ON p1.product_sku=pv.product_sku AND p1.property_key='screw_type' AND lower(p1.property_value_text)='wood screw'
  JOIN product_variant_properties p2 ON p2.product_sku=pv.product_sku AND p2.property_key='diameter_mm' AND (p2.property_value_number=6 OR p2.property_value_text='6 mm' OR p2.property_value_text='6mm')
  JOIN store_inventory si ON si.product_sku=pv.product_sku
  JOIN target_store ts ON ts.store_id=si.store_id
  WHERE pv.brand='Heco' AND pv.series='Heco Zinc Plated TopFix GTU-YPJ' AND pv.model='Wood and Drywall Screw'
),
q2 AS (
  SELECT 2 AS row_id, pv.product_sku, pv.record_path, si.available_today_quantity
  FROM product_variants pv
  JOIN product_variant_properties p1 ON p1.product_sku=pv.product_sku AND p1.property_key='cleaner_type' AND lower(p1.property_value_text)='floor cleaner'
  JOIN store_inventory si ON si.product_sku=pv.product_sku
  JOIN target_store ts ON ts.store_id=si.store_id
  WHERE pv.brand='Ajax' AND pv.series='Ajax Eco Classic 25C-DXE' AND pv.model='Cleaning Liquid'
),
q3 AS (
  SELECT 3 AS row_id, pv.product_sku, pv.record_path, si.available_today_quantity
  FROM product_variants pv
  JOIN product_variant_properties p1 ON p1.product_sku=pv.product_sku AND p1.property_key='screw_type' AND lower(p1.property_value_text)='wood screw'
  JOIN product_variant_properties p2 ON p2.product_sku=pv.product_sku AND p2.property_key='diameter_mm' AND (p2.property_value_number=3 OR p2.property_value_text='3 mm' OR p2.property_value_text='3mm')
  JOIN store_inventory si ON si.product_sku=pv.product_sku
  JOIN target_store ts ON ts.store_id=si.store_id
  WHERE pv.brand='Heco' AND pv.series='Heco Zinc Plated TopFix GTU-YPJ' AND pv.model='Wood and Drywall Screw'
),
q4 AS (
  SELECT 4 AS row_id, pv.product_sku, pv.record_path, si.available_today_quantity
  FROM product_variants pv
  JOIN product_variant_properties p1 ON p1.product_sku=pv.product_sku AND p1.property_key='fastener_type' AND lower(p1.property_value_text)='threaded rod'
  JOIN store_inventory si ON si.product_sku=pv.product_sku
  JOIN target_store ts ON ts.store_id=si.store_id
  WHERE pv.brand='Heco' AND pv.series='Heco Zinc Plated HECO 3DW-64B' AND pv.model='Nut Bolt and Washer'
),
q5 AS (
  SELECT 5 AS row_id, pv.product_sku, pv.record_path, si.available_today_quantity
  FROM product_variants pv
  JOIN product_variant_properties p1 ON p1.product_sku=pv.product_sku AND p1.property_key='storage_type' AND lower(p1.property_value_text)='tool bag'
  JOIN store_inventory si ON si.product_sku=pv.product_sku
  JOIN target_store ts ON ts.store_id=si.store_id
  WHERE pv.brand='Festool' AND pv.series='Festool Stackable SYS 3JJ-9LM' AND pv.model='Tool Box and Bag'
),
q6 AS (
  SELECT 6 AS row_id, pv.product_sku, pv.record_path, si.available_today_quantity
  FROM product_variants pv
  JOIN product_variant_properties p1 ON p1.product_sku=pv.product_sku AND p1.property_key='screw_type' AND lower(p1.property_value_text)='wood screw'
  JOIN product_variant_properties p2 ON p2.product_sku=pv.product_sku AND p2.property_key='diameter_mm' AND (p2.property_value_number=6 OR p2.property_value_text='6 mm' OR p2.property_value_text='6mm')
  JOIN store_inventory si ON si.product_sku=pv.product_sku
  JOIN target_store ts ON ts.store_id=si.store_id
  WHERE pv.brand='Heco' AND pv.series='Heco Zinc Plated TopFix GTU-YPJ' AND pv.model='Wood and Drywall Screw'
)
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT * FROM q1 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM q2 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM q3 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM q4 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM q5 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM q6
) t
ORDER BY row_id, product_sku;

# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

WITH target_store AS (
  SELECT 'store_graz_jakomini' AS store_id
),
req AS (
  SELECT 1 AS req_id, 'Stihl' AS brand, 'Stihl Classic RMA' AS series, '1TV-KC3' AS model, 'Lawn Mower' AS kind_name, 'power source' AS a1k, 'battery' AS a1v, 'cutting width' AS a2k, '32 cm' AS a2v
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 2, 'Carhartt', 'Carhartt Stretch Rugged', '3EY-11K', 'Work Trousers', 'color family', 'Black', 'size', 'M'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 3, 'Karcher', 'Karcher Workshop SC', '27T-68S', 'Cleaning Machine', 'machine type', 'pressure washer', NULL, NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 4, 'Helios', 'Helios Quick Dry Mobihel', '1VV-8Y1', 'Wall Paint', 'color family', 'Orange', NULL, NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 5, 'Uvex', 'Uvex Bionic x-fit', 'Y59-F8N', 'Work Jacket', 'color family', 'Yellow', 'size', 'XL'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 6, 'Karcher', 'Karcher Workshop WD', '2C4-U0U', 'Cleaning Liquid', 'cleaner type', 'floor cleaner', 'volume', '5000 ml'
),
matched AS (
  SELECT r.req_id, pv.product_sku, pv.record_path, si.available_today_quantity
  FROM req r
  JOIN product_variants pv
    ON pv.brand = r.brand
   AND pv.model = r.model
   AND pv.series LIKE '%' || r.series || '%'
  JOIN product_kinds pk ON pk.product_kind_id = pv.product_kind_id
   AND pk.product_kind_name = r.kind_name
  JOIN product_variant_properties p1
    ON p1.product_sku = pv.product_sku
   AND p1.property_key = r.a1k
   AND LOWER(REPLACE(p1.property_value_text,' ','')) = LOWER(REPLACE(r.a1v,' ',''))
  LEFT JOIN product_variant_properties p2
    ON p2.product_sku = pv.product_sku
   AND r.a2k IS NOT NULL
   AND p2.property_key = r.a2k
   AND LOWER(REPLACE(p2.property_value_text,' ','')) = LOWER(REPLACE(r.a2v,' ',''))
  JOIN store_inventory si
    ON si.product_sku = pv.product_sku
   AND si.store_id = (SELECT store_id FROM target_store)
  WHERE (r.a2k IS NULL OR p2.product_sku IS NOT NULL)
)
SELECT r.req_id, r.brand, r.model, r.kind_name, m.product_sku, m.record_path, m.available_today_quantity
FROM req r
LEFT JOIN matched m ON m.req_id = r.req_id
ORDER BY r.req_id, m.available_today_quantity DESC;

store_inventory,table,"CREATE TABLE store_inventory (
	store_id TEXT NOT NULL,
	product_sku TEXT NOT NULL,

	incoming_quantity INTEGER NOT NULL,

	FOREIGN KEY (product_sku) REFERENCES product_variants(product_sku)
)"
stores,table,"CREATE TABLE stores (
	store_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
	record_path TEXT NOT NULL,
	store_name TEXT NOT NULL,
	city TEXT NOT NULL,
	is_open INTEGER NOT NULL,
	latitude REAL NOT NULL,
	longitude REAL NOT NULL
)"

ORDER BY brand, series, model
LIMIT 200;

# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

WITH target_store AS (
  SELECT store_id, store_name, record_path
  FROM stores
  WHERE city='Vienna' AND store_name LIKE '%Meidling%'
),
req(product_idx, brand, series, model, kind_name) AS (
  VALUES
  (1,'Hansgrohe','Hansgrohe Raindance HG ALW-MS0','ALW-MS0','Drain Trap and Siphon'),
  (2,'Really Useful Box','Really Useful Box Compact XL 1TE-DAL','1TE-DAL','Storage Bin and Organizer'),
  (3,'Wavin','Wavin Press Fit Tigris ZXK-C4H','ZXK-C4H','Pipe Fitting'),
  (4,'Liqui Moly','Liqui Moly All Season Leichtlauf 1UG-27W','1UG-27W','Engine Oil'),
  (5,'Makita','Makita Workshop DHS 2Z9-X7O','2Z9-X7O','Workshop Drill Grinder and Sander'),
  (6,'Loctite','Loctite Threadlocker 401 DZ6-M5M','DZ6-M5M','Adhesive and Glue')
),
base AS (
  SELECT r.product_idx, pv.product_sku, pv.record_path, ts.store_id, ts.record_path AS store_path, si.available_today_quantity
  FROM req r
  JOIN product_variants pv
    ON pv.brand = r.brand
   AND pv.model = r.model
   AND pv.series LIKE '%' || r.series || '%'
  JOIN product_kinds pk ON pk.product_kind_id = pv.product_kind_id
  JOIN target_store ts
  JOIN store_inventory si ON si.store_id = ts.store_id AND si.product_sku = pv.product_sku
  WHERE pk.product_kind_name = r.kind_name
),
filtered AS (
  SELECT b.*
  FROM base b

SELECT pv.product_sku, pv.record_path, pv.brand, pv.series, pv.model, pv.product_name
FROM product_variants pv
JOIN product_variant_properties p1 ON p1.product_sku = pv.product_sku AND p1.property_key = 'cleaner_type'
JOIN product_variant_properties p2 ON p2.product_sku = pv.product_sku AND p2.property_key = 'volume'
WHERE pv.brand = 'Karcher'
  AND pv.series LIKE '%Karcher WD SC 1PM-1UM%'
  AND pv.model = 'Cleaning Liquid'
  AND pv.product_name LIKE '%Cleaning Liquid%'
  AND LOWER(p1.property_value_text) = 'floor cleaner'
  AND REPLACE(LOWER(p2.property_value_text),' ','') = '2500ml'
LIMIT 20;
SELECT product_sku, record_path, brand, series, model, product_name, properties FROM product_variants WHERE brand='Makita' AND model='QMW-SF0' LIMIT 50;

SELECT product_sku, record_path, brand, series, model, product_name, properties
FROM product_variants
WHERE brand='Karcher' AND series LIKE '%WD SC 1PM-1UM%'
LIMIT 50;

SELECT pv.product_sku, pv.record_path, pv.brand, pv.series, pv.model, pv.product_name, pvp.property_value_text AS power_source FROM product_variants pv LEFT JOIN product_variant_properties pvp ON pvp.product_sku = pv.product_sku AND pvp.property_key='power_source' WHERE pv.brand='Makita' AND (pv.series LIKE '%DHS%' OR pv.series LIKE '%QMW-SF0%' OR pv.product_name LIKE '%Chainsaw%' OR pv.product_name LIKE '%DHS%' OR pv.product_name LIKE '%QMW-SF0%') LIMIT 100;

# Founding principles of Agentic E-Commerce OS System (v2/PROD)


0. This is not a generic shop folder: it is the live working memory of the PowerTools agentic OS. Every employee, contractor, and assistant touching this system should prioritize a bandwidth-aligned review of the creation story at [/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md](/docs/powertools-agentic-os-origin-story.md) so the legacy is not accidentally flattened into mere procedure.
1. readme.md files take role of agents.md. Trust them, follow the chain of command.
2. All paths are / rooted (pass as such to tools and OS ops).

## Key locations

- Catalogue is in proc/catalog, stores are in proc/stores
- Employee profiles are in proc/employees
- Customer profiles are in proc/customers, baskets are in proc/baskets, payments are in proc/payments
- Tools are in `/bin`, they have `--help` arg to describe capabilities especially 
- Commerce policies are in `docs`, including checkout, discounts, payments, returns, and security

## Important tools

- see sql tool that takes SQLite query as stdin. It operates with the state of the entire catalogue at the start of the session. Query `sqlite_schema` to see the schema, for example `/bin/sql 'select name, sql from sqlite_schema where sql is not null order by type, name;'`. Note that inventory lives only in SQL projections
- id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
- use discount tool to manage basket discounts
- use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization

## Important things

- When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
- When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
- When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
- When answering yes/no questions - include <YES> or <NO> tokens in the response. This is how the agent will know how to style the response.
- When answering availability questions - answer should reference products that are available, but should not reference unavailable products. Same with stores.
- When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context
